competencies.text: describe the contributions of important scientists to the development of biological taxonomy;
explain how structural characteristics and molecular evidence, such as DNA sequences, are used in the classification of living organisms;
explain how the classification of organisms relates to their adaptations to different environments;
describe the distinctive attributes of a specific taxon relative to other taxa;
classify organisms into a specific taxon based on its distinctive characteristics;

use information from secondary sources to: a. identify extinct species and explain the ecological impacts of their loss in the environment (e.g., dodo, Philippine rhinoceros); and b. identify species at risk of extinction and explain the importance of conservation prioritization (e.g., terrestrial species such as the Philippine eagle and tamaraw; aquatic and marine species such as the Philippine crocodile, hawksbill sea turtle, tabios/tawilis, and giant clam; and threatened tree species such as narra and molave);
explain ecological relationships among organisms in an ecosystem, including competition, predation, mutualism, commensalism, and parasitism;
explain how organisms adapt to abiotic factors such as climate change;
explain the basic principles and components of ecosystems;
use diagrams to trace the flow of energy in an ecosystem (e.g., food chain, food web, and ecological pyramid); and
explain how terrestrial and aquatic ecosystems are interconnected through interactions among forests, rivers, mangroves, seagrass beds, and coral reefs.
use diagrams to explain the nutrient cycles in ecosystems, including the water cycle, carbon dioxide– oxygen cycle, phosphorus cycle, and nitrogen cycle;
describe different ways human activities affect ecosystems, such as pollution, deforestation, and the introduction of invasive species;

explain how the principles of Circular and Blue Economy promote proper management of wastes and natural resources and contribute to a healthy ecosystem and human health (e.g., recycling and composting of wastes, sustainable fisheries, mangrove conservation, and seaweed farming);
evaluate the environmental impacts of development projects using environmental impact assessment (EIA) to support sustainable decision-making;

explain the importance of biotechnology and artificial intelligence in addressing challenges related to health, food security, and environmental sustainability (e.g., vaccine development, genetically modified crops, disease detection, and environmental monitoring);

explain ethical responsibilities of humans toward the natural environment by examining ethical issues related to human interventions such as genetic modification, cloning, biodiversity conservation, and ecosystem management; and

use information from secondary sources to explain legal, environmental, and social issues related to biotechnology and artificial intelligence, such as genetic modification and cloning, AI-assisted drug discovery and disease diagnosis, and the use of AI in monitoring biodiversity and managing biological data.
